items.title: The guessing machine
items.brief:
Picture-only sentence game. 0–4 s: many small picture tiles (cups of tea, coffee mugs,
water glasses, bowls of amahewu — tea cups most numerous) stream from the left into a simple
phone-shaped machine. 4–8 s: a half-sentence picture appears (a sunrise + a person + a cup
outline with a question mark). 8–11 s: the machine "thinks" (bubble pulses) and outputs the
most common tile — a teacup — with a confident bounce. 11–14 s: beside it, a learner figure holds
a different drink (amahewu); a small question mark appears between them. 14–16 s: fade back to
the start. No text.

items.title: Good photo, bad photo
items.brief:
Phone camera view of a leaf with holes. 0–3 s: dark, blurry, far away, sun flaring in
the lens. 3–6 s: the photographer turns so the sun (north, top of sky) is behind her — flare
gone. 6–9 s: phone moves close; leaf fills the frame. 9–11 s: a finger taps the leaf — it snaps
sharp. 11–13 s: a flat hand slides in beside the leaf for size; a tick appears. 13–14 s: hold.

items.title: A voice can be copied
items.brief:
0–4 s: a young man records a short voice note; a sound-wave shape leaves his phone.
4–8 s: the wave flies into a shadowy box that stamps out an identical wave. 8–12 s: the copied
wave arrives on his mother's phone from an unknown number with a coin and airtime icon beside it.
12–16 s: she lowers the phone, taps a saved contact with her son's face — the real son answers,
surprised; both shake heads. 16–18 s: a small padlock and a heart (code word) appear. No text.

items.title: Climb the Check Ladder
items.brief:
A farmer with a phone climbs the five-rung ladder from A-P07-ART. As she reaches each
rung (every 2.5 s), its small picture lights up: own garden with sun in the north → circular
arrow → seed packet and label → two people talking → one small row planted. At the top she
smiles and plants the row. Loop.

items.title: The sun is in the north (for "does it make sense here?")
items.brief:
Optional, for rung ① of the Check Ladder: "AI often answers with northern seasons.
Here the sun is in the north, and winter is June–July." Play once, no narration over it.

items.title: Look at the soil
items.brief:
Optional clip for "AI can't see your soil" — people observe soil with their own eyes
and hands. Show on a tablet to groups while they discuss what only people can do.

items.title: What the farm record shows
items.brief:
Optional, before reading an AI-written report: "A report is only as true as your
records. If the record says 12 bunches, the report can't say 50."

items.title: Learning together under a tree
items.brief:
Landscape 16:9. A group of five learners on plastic chairs under a big shade tree near
a small community garden: a gogo, an older man in a hat, two young women, a young man. One
phone is shared between the gogo and a young woman; the young woman points at the screen, the
gogo laughs. The others lean in. A poster on a fence behind (plain shapes, no text). Midday
light, sun high in the north; soft shade. Leave the left third calm (Paper-coloured sky and wall)
for the slide title.

items.title: Where AI hides — picture set
items.brief:
Eight square icons (each 800 × 800 px, plus one sheet with all eight): 1. keyboard
with three blank suggestion bubbles above; 2. keyboard with a microphone key highlighted; 3. a
chat screen with a plain ring icon; 4. phone camera frame over a leaf; 5. two overlapping speech
bubbles with different scribble-scripts; 6. a video feed with a thumb scrolling; 7. incoming-call
screen with a warning triangle; 8. a phone with a garden-app screen and a help strip along the
bottom showing a seedling. Flat, bold, readable at A6. No real logos.

items.title: Weigh it to check it
items.brief:
Landscape 16:9. At a table outside, a young man photographs a bag of carrots and
potatoes with a 2 ℓ plastic water bottle beside it for size. Next to him, an older woman places
the same bag on a simple kitchen scale; the dial pointer is visible (no numbers readable). The
two look at each other, comparing. Station feel: other groups in the background at a bed and
a tree.

items.title: Look at the soil — AI can't
items.brief:
Use the whole image (soil profile beside a jar test). Facilitator says: "AI can look
at a photo. It can't do this — squeeze, smell, shake a jar, count worms."

items.title: The AI desk (facilitator plays the machine)
items.brief:
Landscape 16:9. A facilitator (woman, 30s) sits on a chair at the side of a hall
wearing a large card on a string round her neck — the card shows a simple drawn phone with a
question mark (a drawing, not words). She holds a small stack of cards and reads one in a
deadpan, confident way. A group Reporter (young man) stands in front of her with a notebook; two
learners behind him grin. Playful, warm.

items.title: Share or not — three piles
items.brief:
Top-down view of a reed mat with three sheets: one with a green circle, one with an
orange triangle, one with a red square. Hands of different ages place small cards (blank faces
with small icons: an ID shape, a leaf, a padlock, a pin) onto the piles. No text.

items.title: Lock your chats
items.brief:
Close-up of two hands (an elder's and a youth's) around an entry-level phone. On the
screen: a large padlock over six empty PIN dots, and a toggle switched on. Background soft-focus
garden. No real app interface or logo.

items.title: The family code word
items.brief:
Landscape 16:9. Split scene: left, a mother in her kitchen listening to a voice note,
eyebrow raised, finger to chin (thinking); right, the same mother and her adult son face to face
on the stoep, both smiling, the son whispering something in her ear (agreeing the code word in
person). A thin dotted line joins the two halves.

items.title: Red pen on the draft
items.brief:
Landscape 16:9, top-down. A table with: a printed page of lines (no words) with two
lines crossed out in red and new squiggles written above; a phone showing a chat bubble; a till
slip beside it with a finger tracing a line on the slip; an exercise-book money record open; a
red pen. Hands of a young woman.

items.title: Read the report together
items.brief:
Landscape 16:9. A mentor (man, 40s, programme bib or plain jacket) and a farmer
(woman, 50s) sit on a bench with a printed report (lines and a simple bar-chart shape, no words).
The farmer points at one bar and shakes her head gently; the mentor holds a pen ready to correct.
Garden beds and a harvest crate behind.

items.title: Fair and green AI
items.brief:
Landscape 16:9. Foreground: a small homestead garden with a woman holding a phone,
two speech bubbles above her — one full (English-shaped scribbles), one half-empty (her own
language). Far background, on the horizon: a large windowless grey building with cooling fans,
power lines running to it and a water tower beside it (the data centre). A thin dotted line runs
from the phone to the far building. Calm, not scary.

items.title: Certificate day
items.brief:
Landscape 16:9. A facilitator shakes hands with a proud gogo holding a certificate
(blank paper with a simple border and a seal shape, no text); a youth beside her claps; other
learners in a semicircle holding their own. Posters on the wall behind (shapes only).

items.title: Screen: the Lima help strip
items.brief:
Screenshot captured on Day 0 from a **sample/demo account** (no real farmer data):
ImbewuField Home with the Lima help strip at the bottom, then Lima answering a Question-Hand
question about spinach holes. Crop to the phone frame. Recapture before each course if the
screen has changed. Blur anything personal.

items.title: Plant problem photographs (6)
items.brief:
Six real photographs, taken in South African gardens with the grower's consent, no
people's faces: holes in spinach leaves; yellowing lower leaves on maize; seedlings collapsed at
the soil line (damping off) in a tray; aphids clustered under a cabbage leaf; termite-eaten mulch
around a bed; frost-burnt leaf tips. Clear, close, good light, a hand or matchbox for size.
Printed A5 for the no-phone path.

items.title: Screen: Lima Vision result
items.brief:
Two screenshots from a demo account: "What's growing" result (crop, rough kg, weeks
to harvest, confidence pill) and "Weigh my harvest" result (estimated kg, confidence pill).
Use a real test photo of a bed and of produce beside a 2 ℓ bottle.

items.title: Screen: Tree ID result
items.brief:
Screenshot of a Tree ID result for a common tree (demo account), showing the
confidence number and the note. Choose an example where the confidence is **not** 100% — it
teaches that confidence varies.

items.title: Screen: till slip read in Records → Spent
items.brief:
Side-by-side: a photo of a real till slip (an invented or blurred shop name, no card
numbers) and the Records → Spent entry after "scan a till slip" showing total, item and shop. If
possible use an example where the reader made a small mistake (e.g. read the change as the
total) — mark it with a red circle added on the slide, not in the screenshot.

items.title: Screen: an AI-written report
items.brief:
Screenshot of a Reports page generated for a demo garden. Crop to one paragraph and
one chart. No real names or locations.

items.title: Our class and phone agreement
items.headline: Learn together, phones too
items.labels:
1. Phones silent, not away
2. Share the turn
3. Ask before photos
4. Private stays private
items.layout:
Headline top band; art 45%; labels as numbered callouts; a 20% blank panel with
ruled lines for the class's own rules (marker on paper, or a sheet taped on the banner).
items.teach_it:
```
A-P01  Our class and phone agreement            (≈ 8 min)
1. GROUPS: agree one rule that helps us learn together. 2 min.
2. Reporters say it; Recorder writes/draws it in the blank panel.
3. POINT ①: phones silent, not away — we use them in class.
4. POINT ②: one phone, many people — everyone gets a turn.
5. POINT ③: ask before you photograph a person (POPIA consent).
6. POINT ④: no ID, PIN or bank details typed today.
7. ASK: Can we all live with these? Thumbs up.
KEY: We share phones, we share turns, we protect each other.
```

items.title: AI is a guessing machine
items.headline: AI is a fast guesser
items.labels:
1. Learned from lots
2. Guesses what's next
3. Sure, but wrong
4. Knows what you show
items.layout: Headline top; art 60% flowing left to right; labels under the art in the callout band.
items.teach_it:
```
A-P02  AI is a guessing machine                  (≈ 20 min with the role-play)
1. PLAY: "Finish my sentence" — 3 starts, room shouts, tally the answers.
2. Put on the AI sign. Answer with the most common word, every time.
3. Ask the machine about a coughing goat — answer fast, sure, and unsafe.
4. Ask it when to plant maize — answer "April" (northern seasons).
5. Take the sign off: "Now I'm me again."
6. POINT ①→④ and say each label.
7. ASK: What doesn't it know about your farm?
KEY: AI is a very fast guesser. Very good is not always right.
```

items.title: Where you already meet AI
items.headline: AI is already here
items.labels:
1. Keyboard guesses words
2. Voice typing
3. Chat helper
4. Camera search
5. Translate
6. Garden app helper
items.layout: Headline top; phone centre with islands around; labels in a 2 × 3 grid at the foot.
items.teach_it:
```
A-P03  Where you already meet AI                 (≈ 12 min)
1. SAY: You've probably used AI this week. Let's find it.
2. GROUPS with a phone: find 3 places AI is on your phone.
3. EVERYONE: type "Good m…" and watch the keyboard guess ①.
4. GROUPS: sort the picture cards — used / not used.
5. Reporters name one each; tick the island on the poster.
6. ASK: Which one surprised you?
KEY: You already use AI — keyboard, mic, camera, chat.
```

items.title: Save your data
items.headline: Make your data last
items.labels:
1. Auto-download off
2. Standard photos
3. Data saver on
4. Updates on Wi-Fi
5. Voice, not video
items.layout: Headline top; the pot centre; five callouts in a ring; labels in the band below.
items.teach_it:
```
A-P04  Save your data                            (≈ 20 min)
1. ASK: What did you spend on data last week? Tell your neighbour.
2. Connect the group phone to the course Wi-Fi.
3. ① WhatsApp › Settings › Storage and data › Media auto-download › mobile data: none.
4. ② Photo upload quality › Standard.
5. ③ Phone Settings › search "data saver" › on.
6. ④ Play Store › auto-update on Wi-Fi only.
7. ⑤ Habit: voice notes use less data than video.
KEY: Learners tap it themselves. Menus differ — use Settings search.
```

items.title: The Question Hand
items.headline: Ask with your whole hand
items.labels:
1. Who I am
2. What I have
3. What I want
4. How to answer
5. Ask again
items.layout: Headline top; the hand fills 60%; labels as callouts beside each finger (large, 64 pt).
items.teach_it:
```
A-P05  The Question Hand                         (≈ 15 min + practice)
1. AI sign on. A learner asks one word: "Spinach?" Read B-00 — long, useless.
2. Sign off. Hold up your hand: "A good question has five fingers."
3. POINT ①–⑤ with an example: farmer near Bergville · spinach bed with holes ·
   stop it · 3 short steps in isiZulu · ask again.
4. AI sign on. Ask the full question. Read B-01 — short, useful.
5. ASK: Which answer helps more? Why?
6. PAIRS: say the five fingers in your own language.
KEY: Tell it who you are and what you have. The first answer is a draft.
```

items.title: Ask with your voice and a photo
items.headline: Say it. Show it.
items.labels:
1. Light behind you
2. Close up
3. Hold still
4. One thing
5. Show the size
6. Speak, then read
items.layout: Headline top; art split 25% voice / 35% photo; callouts beside; labels band.
items.teach_it:
```
A-P06  Ask with your voice and a photo           (≈ 7 min + stations)
1. ENERGISER: Broken Telephone — a farm sentence whispered round the circle.
2. SHOW: keyboard mic ⑥. Speak a question. Read what it wrote.
3. PAIRS: English, then first language. Fix mistakes.
4. SHOW two photos: dark and blurry vs clear. ASK: which can AI understand?
5. POINT ①–⑤. Add: both sides of a sick leaf, and the whole plant.
6. Ask before a person is in your photo.
KEY: Clear photo, better answer. A photo answer is still a guess — check it.
```

items.title: The Check Ladder
items.headline: Check before you trust
items.labels:
1. Makes sense here?
2. Ask again
3. Second source
4. Ask a person
5. Try it small
items.layout: Headline top; ladder rising left to right across 60%; labels next to each rung.
items.teach_it:
```
A-P07  The Check Ladder                          (≈ 8 min + Find the mistakes)
1. AI sign on: "Plant cabbage 5 cm apart." ASK: Would you do it? How did you know?
2. ASK: In the village, how do you check a rumour?
3. POINT ①→⑤ bottom to top; a learner says each rung in their language.
4. SAY: How high you climb depends on how bad a mistake would be (A-P08).
5. GROUPS: Find the mistakes — 4 B-cards; circle, colour, who to ask.
6. Reporters share one mistake each.
KEY: Makes sense? · ask again · second source · ask a person · try small.
```

items.title: Green · Orange · Red questions
items.headline: How bad if it's wrong?
items.labels:
1. Green: try small
2. Orange: check again
3. Red: danger
4. Red? Ask a person
items.layout: Headline top; three panels 60%; labels to the right of each panel.
items.teach_it:
```
A-P08  Green · Orange · Red                       (≈ 10 min)
1. POINT ① green: ideas, recipes, names, writing help — try it small.
2. POINT ② orange: planting dates, spacing, pests, prices — second source.
3. POINT ③ red: sprays and poisons, medicine, animal health, loans, grants,
   SASSA, contracts, land — ④ always a person. Never AI alone.
4. GROUPS: sort T-01…T-12 onto the three sheets. 6 min.
5. ASK groups: "What's the worst that could happen?"
KEY: The label is the law. Red questions go to a person.
```

items.title: Keep it private
items.headline: Your phone is your wallet
items.labels:
1. ID number
2. Bank card, PIN
3. Codes (OTPs)
4. Grant details
5. Children's faces
6. Where you are
items.layout:
Headline top; wallet 55%; "Never share" as a small Ochre tag above the six labels.
(The tag is 2 more words — total stays ≤ 25.)
items.teach_it:
```
A-P09  Keep it private                            (≈ 20 min with the sort)
1. ASK: What's in your wallet you'd never give a stranger?
2. SAY: Your phone is a wallet now.
3. GROUPS: sort the H-cards — fine / trusted face to face / never. 10 min.
4. POINT ①–⑥: never share with strangers or AI.
5. SAY (POPIA): the law protects your information; you can ask what an
   organisation holds and complain to the Information Regulator.
6. SAY: AI apps may keep what you type. Ask about spinach, not your bank.
KEY: Codes and PINs: never, to anyone.
```

items.title: Stop · Check · Ask
items.headline: Stop · Check · Ask
items.labels:
1. Don't click, pay, send
2. Call back, known number
3. Ask someone you trust
items.layout: Headline top; three panels 50%; warning-icon strip 15%; labels under the panels.
items.teach_it:
```
A-P10  Stop · Check · Ask                          (≈ 5 min + scam cards)
1. PLAY the fake voice note (Day 0 recording). ASK: What would you do?
2. POINT ①: STOP — scammers rush you.
3. POINT ②: CHECK — call back on the number you already have.
4. POINT ③: ASK — family, mentor, bank at the branch, SASSA office, police.
5. POINT the warning strip: hurry · secret · money/airtime/code · too good ·
   a link · pay a fee for a job, grant or loan.
6. GROUPS: sort S-01…S-10 — scam / real / not sure. 15 min.
KEY: Hurry + money or code = scam until proven real.
```

items.title: Fake voices, fake videos
items.headline: Voices and videos can lie
items.labels:
1. Voices can be copied
2. Too good? Too scary?
3. Call back yourself
4. Family code word
items.layout: Headline top; art in three panels 60%; labels in the band.
items.teach_it:
```
A-P11  Fake voices, fake videos                   (≈ 15 min)
1. SAY: AI can copy a voice from a short voice note, and make a video of a
   famous person saying things they never said.
2. ASK: How can you tell? Collect answers.
3. POINT ①–④.
4. SAY: Check the message, not the picture. Money, secrets or codes = stop.
5. PAIRS: role-play a family member "in trouble"; the other asks the code question.
6. SAY: agree the code word face to face. Never write it down or post it.
KEY: Call back on the number you know. Use a family code word.
```

items.title: AI drafts, you own it
items.headline: AI drafts. You own it.
items.labels:
1. Facts true?
2. Sounds like me?
3. Nothing private?
4. Would I sign it?
items.layout: Headline top; art 60%; four checks as a checklist band with tick boxes.
items.teach_it:
```
A-P12  AI drafts, you own it                      (≈ 8 min + practical)
1. ENERGISER: Human or Machine? — read D-00, stand/sit.
2. POINT ①–④: the four checks before you send.
3. SAY: CVs, funding requests, reports carry YOUR name. Never send what isn't true.
4. GROUPS: draft with AI (or use a D-sheet), then red-pen it.
5. [APP] till slip: check total, item, shop against the paper. The slip wins.
6. Two groups read their fixed version aloud.
KEY: AI drafts, you own it — every fact, every word.
```

items.title: What AI can't do
items.headline: Only people can do this
items.labels:
1. Feel your soil
2. Measure the rain
3. Elders' knowledge
4. Your mentor
5. Our languages — double-check
items.layout: Headline top; scene 60% with the small dark phone near the centre; labels in the band.
items.teach_it:
```
A-P13  What AI can't do                          (≈ 15 min)
1. SAY: Hands up if AI can do it, down if it can't.
2. ASK: see your soil? replace a soil test or scale? know your rain?
   know today's market price? know your gogo's knowledge? replace your mentor?
   sign for you?  — give the one-line answer each time.
3. POINT ①–④.
4. GROUPS: agree one thing only people can do; Recorder adds it beside the poster.
5. POINT ⑤: AI is weaker in isiZulu and Sesotho — double-check (Day 2 S4).
KEY: AI can't see your soil or feel the rain. People, land and elders first.
```

items.title: My AI plan
items.headline: Use it to think. Ask to decide.
items.labels:
1. Use AI for
2. Always ask a person
3. My data rule
4. My safety step
5. I will teach
items.layout:
Headline top (two short lines); art 55%; labels match the K-06 plan sheet line by
line, so learners can copy the shape.
items.teach_it:
```
A-P14  My AI plan                                 (≈ 15 min)
1. Hand out K-06. Point to ①–⑤ — the plan has the same five parts.
2. Learners fill it alone — words or drawings. 8 min.
3. REMIND: never write your family code word.
4. PAIRS: tell your plan; partner asks "What will you do first?"
5. Invite 2–3 volunteers to say one line to the room.
KEY: Use AI to think; ask a person to decide.
```

items.title: Artwork for A-P01 · Our class and phone agreement
items.brief:
A circle of eight seated learners of mixed ages and genders under a
tree — a gogo with a headscarf, a young man in a cap, a young woman, an older man with a
walking stick. Two pairs lean over one shared phone together, smiling. A third phone lies
face-down on a knee (silent). One young woman holds up a hand to a person with a phone camera,
palm out, polite ("ask first"). A small padlock floats above one phone. Four numbered callout
circles: ① on the face-down phone, ② on a shared screen, ③ on the raised hand, ④ on the padlock.
Lower third of the poster left empty (paper colour) for the group's own rules written on the day.

items.title: Artwork for A-P02 · AI is a guessing machine
items.brief:
Centre: a friendly, simple machine made of a phone shape with a big
thought bubble. Left side feeding into it: a tall stream of many small paper pages, books and
photographs flying in (the training). Right side coming out: three speech bubbles; the top one
has a big tick shape, the middle one a tick, the bottom one a cross — but all three bubbles look
equally bold and confident. Below the machine, a small homestead garden (beds, a goat, a water
tank) sits behind a closed gate — the machine can't see into it. A farmer (middle-aged woman,
gumboots) stands at the gate holding a phone, about to "show" the garden. Callouts: ① on the
stream of pages, ② on the machine's thought bubble, ③ on the confident bubble with the cross,
④ on the closed gate.

items.title: Artwork for A-P03 · Where you already meet AI
items.brief:
One large phone in the centre, drawn slightly tilted, held in a
youth's hand. Around it, six icon "islands" joined to the phone by dotted lines: a keyboard with
three suggestion bubbles above it; a microphone; a chat bubble with a small round ring icon; a
camera frame over a leaf; two overlapping speech bubbles (translation); a small seedling in a
circle (the garden app's helper). An elder sits beside the youth, looking on, pointing at the
keyboard island. Callouts ①–⑥ on the six islands.

items.title: Artwork for A-P04 · Save your data
items.brief:
A phone drawn as a clay water pot (a data "pot") with a small tap at
the bottom; a few drops fall from it. Around it: ① a photo/video icon with a pause symbol
(auto-download off), ② a small photo next to a big photo, the small one ticked (standard
quality), ③ a gauge/dial turned to low (data saver), ④ a Wi-Fi fan-shape over a download arrow
(updates on Wi-Fi only), ⑤ a voice-note waveform next to a video icon, the waveform smaller.
A young woman holds the phone-pot carefully with two hands. Water blue only for the drops.

items.title: Artwork for A-P05 · The Question Hand
items.brief:
One big open right hand, palm facing the viewer, brown skin, a farm-
worker's hand (a little soil on the fingertips). Beside each finger a small picture: thumb — a
simple farmer figure pointing at herself (who I am); pointer — a bed with plants and a water
drum (what I have); middle — a target with a seedling in the centre (what I want); ring — three
short stacked bars like steps, and a speech bubble (how to answer); little finger — a circular
arrow (ask again). Callouts ①–⑤ on the fingers from thumb to little finger.

items.title: Artwork for A-P06 · Ask with your voice and a photo
items.brief:
Top half: an older man speaking into a phone held near his mouth, a
sound-wave shape flowing into the phone; a small keyboard with a microphone key glows. Bottom
half: a young woman crouched by a bed, photographing a single leaf with holes. Sun behind her
in the **north** (upper part of the sky, compass rose in the corner showing N up), her shadow
falling away from the sun, not on the leaf. Beside the leaf, her other hand spread flat for size.
Five callouts on the bottom half: ① the sun behind her, ② the phone close to the leaf, ③ both
her hands steady, ④ one single leaf, ⑤ the hand for size. One callout ⑥ on the talking man.

items.title: Artwork for A-P07 · The Check Ladder
items.brief:
A wooden ladder leaning against a water tank, five rungs. A farmer
(woman, 40s, headscarf, gumboots) climbs it holding a phone. Beside each rung, a small picture:
bottom rung — the farmer's own garden with the sun in the north (does it make sense here?);
second — a circular arrow around a speech bubble (ask again); third — a seed packet and a
product bottle with a label, side by side (second source); fourth — two people talking, one an
extension officer with a clipboard (ask a person); top rung — a single small row of plants
inside a big empty bed (try it small). Callouts ①–⑤ bottom to top.

items.title: Artwork for A-P08 · Green · Orange · Red questions
items.brief:
Three stacked panels like a traffic light, each also marked with a
shape so it works in black and white: **green circle** panel — a pot of food cooking and a
seed packet (low harm); **orange triangle** panel — a bed of wilting seedlings and a coin
(could cost a crop or money); **red square** panel — a spray bottle, a medicine bottle, a goat
lying down, and a document with a signature line (poison, medicine, animals, money and papers).
Beside the red panel, two people talking face to face — a farmer and a person in an extension
officer's jacket. Callouts ① ② ③ on the three panels, ④ on the two people.

items.title: Artwork for A-P09 · Keep it private
items.brief:
A phone drawn as an open wallet/purse. Inside it, six items each

items.title: Our class agreement
items.headline: How we learn together
items.labels:
1. Our agreement (above the lines)
2. Sign here (small, beside a row of 30 empty thumb-print circles at the bottom)
items.layout:
Headline top; art band 35%; 12 ruled lines with a pale Leaf tint for writing;
30 thumb-print circles along the bottom edge.
items.teach_it:
1. ASK: "What do we need from each other so everybody can learn?"
2. Write their words — not yours. Hand the marker to a learner.
3. Make sure these are there: phones silent · one voice at a time · right to pass · no laughing
   at anyone · everyone does the practicals · on time · what's personal stays here · respect
   the land.
4. Everyone signs or thumb-prints a circle.
KEY: If we forget, anyone can point to this poster.

items.title: Earth care · People care · Fair share
items.headline: Three ways to care
items.labels:
1. Earth care — soil, water, life
2. People care — family first
3. Fair share — give back the extra
4. All three together (centre)
items.layout:
Headline top; Venn fills 60%; labels outside each circle with a leader line.
Question strip: *"Which one do you already do?"*
items.teach_it:
1. Tell the story of Gogo Thandi and her neighbour (day-1.md S1).
2. ASK: who cared for soil? for people? who shared?
3. Point ① ② ③. One sentence each.
4. GROUPS: draw one thing you already do for each circle (8 min).
5. Reporters: one circle each.
KEY: Earth care, people care, fair share — together, not one at a time.

items.title: Two gardens
items.headline: Which garden will feed you in a drought?
items.labels:
1. Soil always covered
2. Many plants together
3. Water slowed and kept
4. Nothing wasted
items.layout:
Headline top; split art 60% (left slightly desaturated); numbered callouts ①–④ on
the right side only; question strip: *"What did your grandmother do?"*
items.teach_it:
1. Cover the right half. GROUPS: what will this garden look like in a drought? (3 min)
2. Reveal the right half. ASK: what is different?
3. Water-pour demo: bare brick vs mulched brick.
4. SAY: agroecology = farming with nature; permaculture = designing with nature.
5. Point ①–④.
KEY: Bare soil loses water and soil. Covered soil keeps both.

items.title: Six garden principles
items.headline: Six ways to garden with nature
items.labels:
1. Watch first
2. Catch and keep
3. Many helpers
4. Nothing is waste
5. Start small
6. Use the edges
items.layout:
Headline; 6-icon grid 70%; each label directly under its icon; blank flipchart
beside the poster for the magazine hunt.
items.teach_it:
1. For each icon: point, say the principle, ASK for one local example (2 min each).
2. GROUPS: magazine hunt — glue pictures under the six symbols (20 min).
3. Gallery walk; each Reporter explains one surprising match.
KEY: Watch first · catch and keep · many helpers · nothing is waste · start small · use the edges.

items.layout:
Landscape; headline top-left; art 75%; a legend column on the right with the five

items.teach_it:
1. Cardboard house in the sun: where is the shadow? (south) In winter? (longer)

3. GROUPS: site walk with yellow / red / blue ribbons (20 min).
4. Point to the zones: what you use every day goes by the door.

1. ASK: how do we find a line where water stands still?
2. Point ①–③ while groups build (20 min, one frame per group).
3. Calibrate: mark · flip · mark · middle (show once, every group does it).
4. Day 2: one foot on the peg, swing the other until the string hits the middle; peg; move.
KEY: Water on a level line stops and soaks in. Always calibrate.

items.title: Slow · Spread · Sink · Store
items.headline: Make the rain walk, not run
items.labels:
1. Slow it
2. Spread it
3. Sink it
4. Store it
5. Soil is the biggest tank
6. Greywater to trees, not leaves
items.layout:
Landscape; four bands across the top; flow art 70%; question strip: *"What is
the biggest tank on your land?"*
items.teach_it:
1. ASK: where did last summer's storm water go?
2. Tray demo: bare vs stones + grass (each group pours).
3. Walk the poster from roof to soil: ① ② ③ ④.
4. GROUPS: mark two water catches on every garden map.
KEY: Slow · spread · sink · store. Cover the soil — it is your biggest tank.

items.title: How much rain from your roof?
items.headline: 1 mm on 1 m² = 1 litre
items.labels:
1. Length × width = m²
2. × rain (mm) × 0.8
3. = litres caught
4. First rain goes out
5. Lid on
6. Overflow to the garden
items.layout:
Headline as a big equation; three bands (rule 25% · house 35% · tank 30%); a
blank white box (A4 size) where the facilitator writes the venue's own sum in marker.
items.teach_it:
1. Show the 1 ℓ bottle: 1 mm on 1 m² = 1 litre.
2. A 20 mm storm on 1 m² = one 20 ℓ bucket.
3. GROUPS: measure the venue roof on the ground.
4. Worked example: 10 × 6 = 60 m² · × 20 mm × 0.8 = 960 ℓ ≈ 48 buckets.
5. Counters method for anyone who prefers: one bottle top = 1 m² = 1 bucket.
6. Tank parts: gutter, first-flush, lid, tap, overflow.
KEY: Roof area × rain × 0.8 = the water you can catch.

items.title: A swale on the level line
items.headline: Catch the rain on the slope
items.labels:
1. Ditch on the level line
2. Soil below (mound)
3. Water soaks in
4. Plant the mound
5. Safe spillway
items.layout:
Headline; cross-section 60%; inset 20% top-right; question strip: *"Where at home
does water run away?"*
items.teach_it:
1. Safety: points down, nobody behind a pick, drink water, swap every 10 min.
2. Point ①–⑤.
3. GROUPS: mark the contour (everyone places the frame once), dig ditch above pegs, soil below.
4. Test with two 2 ℓ bottles: does water spread or run?
5. Mulch the mound.
KEY: Ditch on the level, soil below, safe spillway. Not on steep slopes.

items.title: Soil is alive
items.headline: Feed the soil, the soil feeds the plant
items.labels:
1. Squeeze
2. Jar
3. Smell and look
4. Count worms
5. Sand · Loam · Clay
6. 10+ worms = healthy
items.layout:
Headline; cut-away 55%; 4 test panels in a row 30%; question strip: *"What does
your soil need?"* (answer on the back: organic matter).
items.teach_it:
1. Two handfuls: alive vs dead soil — how do you know?
2. SAY: one handful of healthy soil holds more life than there are people in SA.
3. GROUPS: four tests, 7 min each (squeeze · jar · smell · worms + tin soak test).
4. Reporters: "Our soil is ___, it needs ___."
KEY: Sandy or clay — the answer is organic matter. Worms are free workers.

items.title: Build a compost heap
items.headline: Waste into food
items.labels:
1. Green (food)
2. Brown (bread) ×2–3
3. Water — like a squeezed cloth
4. Air — sticks and turning
5. 1 m × 1 m × 1 m
6. Warm stick = working
items.layout:
Headline; heap 55% left + four need icons stacked right; bottom strip 20%; small
"never in the heap" row of crossed icons (bone, bottle, tin, oil, plastic bag).
items.teach_it:
1. Energiser: Compost Heap (green sit, brown stand, water wave, air jump).
2. Point the four needs; brown 2–3 : green 1.
3. GROUPS: build (30 min) — sticks, then brown / green / manure / soil / water, repeat.
4. Squeeze test; stick in the middle; cover.
5. Turn after a week; ready in 2–3 months.
KEY: Green + brown + water + air = compost.

items.title: Liquid manure & worm farm
items.headline: Plant food you can pour
items.labels:
1. Manure in a sack
2. 2 weeks, stir
3. 1 cup + 10 cups water
4. On the soil
5. Red compost worms
6. Shade, damp, no citrus
items.layout: Headline; two equal halves separated by a Hairline rule.
items.teach_it:
1. Liquid manure: each group does one step (sack, hang, fill, lid, who stirs).
2. SAY: 2 weeks; 1 cup to 10 cups water; soil not leaves; every 2 weeks.
3. Worm farm: each group one step (holes, bedding, worms, peels, sack).
4. Rules: shade, damp, no citrus/onion/meat/oil.
KEY: Liquid manure 1 : 10 on the soil. Worms make the best compost.

items.title: Beds that hold water
items.headline: Dig once, feed for years
items.labels:
1. 1 m wide — never step in
2. 50–60 cm deep
3. Layers like a sandwich
4. Subsoil in the middle
5. Mulch on top
6. Keyhole bed
items.layout: Headline; trench cut-away 60%; keyhole 30%.
items.teach_it:
1. Point ①–⑤: 1 m wide, deep, layers, topsoil on top, mulch.
2. GROUPS: peg 1 m × 2 m; dig — topsoil one side, subsoil the other (rotate every 10 min).
3. Layer: coarse → manure → green → dry → soil → water; repeat.
4. Top 15 cm: topsoil + compost; lip at the edges; mulch; water.
5. Hard ground? Build a no-dig raised bed on cardboard.
KEY: Deep layered beds hold water and food for years. 1 m wide, never step on it.

items.title: Grow strong seedlings
items.headline: A strong start
items.labels:
1. Sow straight / sow in trays
2. 1 compost : 1 sand : 1 soil
3. Twice as deep as the seed
4. Damp, light shade
5. Harden off 1 week
6. Plant out at 4–6 leaves
items.layout: Three columns; headline across the top.
items.teach_it:
1. Sort crops: straight in the bed vs seedlings first.
2. GROUPS: sieve and mix 1:1:1.
3. Every learner fills and sows their own tray (2 seeds per hole).
4. Label, water, shade.
5. Care: morning water; harden off; transplant late afternoon.
KEY: Twice as deep as the seed. Harden off, then transplant.

items.title: Planting plan: spacing & rotation
items.headline: The right place, the right distance
items.labels:
1. 10 cm · onion, beetroot
2. 30 cm · spinach, lettuce
3. 45 cm · cabbage, tomato
4. Triangle pattern
5. Beans → Leaves → Fruits → Roots
items.layout:
Headline; bed plan 55% with a spacing table box (the four rows from day-4.md);
rotation wheel 40%.
items.teach_it:
1. ASK: too close? too far?
2. GROUPS: make a spacing stick (notches every 10 cm; 15, 30, 45 marked).
3. Plan the bed on paper: 3+ crops; facilitator checks.
4. Mark with the stick, transplant, sow, water, mulch.
5. Rotation: four learners walk the wheel.
KEY: Plan on paper, use the stick, mix crops, rotate every season.

items.title: Healthy garden, fewer pests
items.headline: Climb the ladder from the bottom
items.labels:
1. Healthy soil
2. Many plants
3. Look twice a week
4. Hands and barriers
5. Invite friends
6. Home-made spray
7. Bought poison — last
items.layout:
Headline; ladder 80% with labels on the left of each rung and scenes on the right;
recipe box at the bottom-right: garlic + chilli + onion + water + soap; 1 cup : 4 cups.
items.teach_it:
1. Bug hunt: one pest and one friend per group (15 min).
2. Climb the ladder bottom to top. ASK: where do most people start?
3. GROUPS: make the spray; label it; gloves; wash hands.
4. Collars round seedlings; a board for slugs.
KEY: Start at the bottom. Every pest has an enemy — invite the friends.

items.title: Food-forest layers & planting a fruit tree
items.headline: Plant like a forest
items.labels:
1. Tall tree · small tree · bush
2. Herbs · ground cover · roots · climber
3. 60 × 60 × 60 cm
4. Same depth as the bag
5. Basin, stake, mulch
items.layout: Headline; forest 55%; 6-step strip 40%.
items.teach_it:
1. Name the seven layers; ASK who waters the forest.
2. GROUPS: each group one planting step (pit, mix, depth, plant, basin + stake, water + mulch).
3. SAY: best at the start of the rains; water weekly in the first dry season.
KEY: Layers look after each other. Same depth, basin, mulch.

items.title: Save your seed
items.headline: Seed is life — keep it
items.labels:
1. Open-pollinated — save it
2. Hybrid (F1) — don't
3. Dry method
4. Wet method
5. Cool, dark, dry, labelled
6. 8 of 10 sprout = good
items.layout: Headline; three horizontal bands.
items.teach_it:
1. ASK: where did your grandmother get seed?
2. Open-pollinated vs F1; treated seed is poison.
3. Choose the best, from many plants.
4. GROUPS: dry method (beans) and wet method (tomato); show the 2-day ferment.
5. Store: jar, ash, label. Test 10 seeds.
6. Seed swap: take 5, bring back double.
KEY: Save from the best, from many. Cool, dark, dry, labelled.

items.title: Eat the rainbow
items.headline: The garden on the plate
items.labels:
1. Half: vegetables & fruit
2. Quarter: pap, bread, potato
3. Quarter: beans, eggs, fish, meat
4. Dark green every day
5. Orange for eyes & health
items.layout:
Headline; plate 55%; family around it; colour icons strip; question strip:
*"Which colour is missing in your home?"*
items.teach_it:
1. Point the plate: half, quarter, quarter.
2. The colours: green (iron), orange (vitamin A), beans (growing), red/purple and fruit.
3. GROUPS: plate game with 16 food cards (3 plates for a family with a small child).
4. GROUPS: summer and winter crops for each colour.
5. Harvest, weigh, record: eaten / shared / sold.
KEY: Half the plate vegetables and fruit; dark green and orange every day.

items.title: Money in, money out
items.headline: The garden has its own pocket
items.labels:
1. House · Garden · Savings
2. Money in
3. Money out
4. Write it the same day
5. Cost per bunch first
items.layout: Headline; tins 35%; book 35%; price sum 20%.
items.teach_it:
1. Two pockets: house money, garden money.
2. GROUPS: market-day cards with play money and 3 tins.
3. Everyone writes the lines on the money page; add up.
4. Worked price: R100 ÷ 40 bunches = R2.50 each; compare the spaza price.
KEY: Garden money has its own pocket. Write every rand, the same day.

items.title: My 90-day garden plan
items.headline: My next 90 days
items.labels:
1. First 2 weeks
2. By 6 weeks
3. By 90 days
4. My buddy
items.layout:
Headline; path art 60% with writing boxes; an A4 version is the learner's plan
sheet.
items.teach_it:
1. Read the example plan (day-5.md S4).
2. Everyone fills 2–3 actions per stone (drawing fine).
3. 2 minutes each to the group; two stars and a wish.
4. Choose a buddy; write the name.
KEY: Small steps, written down, checked by a buddy.

items.title: Artwork for F-P01 · Our class agreement
items.brief:
A circle of 10 seated people seen from slightly above — mixed ages,
a gogo in a headscarf, a young man in a cap, a woman with a baby on her back — each with an
open hand towards the middle, where a single seedling grows from a small mound. Keep the art in
the top 35% so the lower part is a **blank ruled area** (12 lines) for the class to write on.

items.title: Artwork for F-P02 · Earth care · People care · Fair share
items.brief:
Three equal overlapping circles (a Venn). Circle ① (top-left, Leaf
green): two cupped hands holding dark soil with a sprouting seedling and an earthworm. Circle
② (top-right, Ochre): a family of four — gogo, mother, two children — eating from one pot.
Circle ③ (bottom, Water blue outline only, Paper fill): one hand passing a basket of
vegetables and a small seed packet to another hand, with a curved arrow back to soil. In the
centre overlap: a small homestead garden.

items.title: Artwork for F-P03 · Two gardens
items.brief:
Split vertically. **Left:** a bare, cracked, pale plot on a slight
slope; one crop in straight rows; a fertiliser bag and a spray can with a skull-free generic
warning shape; rainwater running off in brown channels taking soil down the slope; a hot sun in
the north (upper edge) and a wilting plant. **Right:** the same slope with dark mulched beds,
many mixed plant shapes of different heights, a small tree, a compost heap, a swale with water
soaking in, a tank on a small roof, a bird and a ladybird. Same sky; right side looks cooler.

items.title: Artwork for F-P04 · Six garden principles
items.brief:
A 2 × 3 grid of six square icons with a bold simple scene each:
① a person squatting, watching rain run across a yard (an eye motif); ② a roof gutter pouring
into a tank, and a hand holding seeds; ③ a maize stalk, a bean vine climbing it, and a pumpkin
at its foot; ④ vegetable peels going into a compost heap, a small arrow round to a green plant;
⑤ one small, lush, well-kept bed next to three large bare ones (crossed out lightly); ⑥ a bed
along a path and a fence with climbing beans, a tap dripping onto a plant.

items.title: Artwork for F-P05 · Read your land
items.brief:
A bird's-eye illustrated homestead on a gentle slope. A compass
rose with the N arrow pointing to the TOP of the poster. The sun drawn at the top (north)
with its arc from east (right) to west (left); the house casts its shadow to the SOUTH
(bottom). Blue arrows show water running from the road and roof down the slope. A cold wind
drawn as grey curved lines from the south-west (bottom-left). Five concentric soft bands
around the house (zones 0–5): 0 house; 1 herbs and a tap next to the kitchen door; 2 beds,
fruit trees, a chicken run; 3 a maize/bean/pumpkin field; 4 grazing and a woodlot; 5 wild
bush on the far edge.

items.title: Artwork for F-P06 · Build an A-frame
items.brief:
Large side view of an A-frame made of two wooden droppers tied at
the top (crossed, tips sticking out), a horizontal crossbar halfway, and a string with a stone
hanging from the apex past the crossbar. Below it, a small 3-step strip: (a) frame on two
pegs, a mark where the string crosses; (b) the frame turned round, feet swapped, a second mark;
(c) a big mark exactly between them. At the bottom, a young woman and an older man walking the
frame across a slope, leaving a line of pegs that curves with the land.

items.title: Artwork for F-P07 · Slow · Spread · Sink · Store
items.brief:
A homestead cross-section on a slope, left (top of slope) to right
(bottom). Rain falls on a corrugated-iron roof → gutter → a first-flush pipe → a round covered
tank with a tap and an overflow pipe → the overflow leads into a swale with a mound planted
with small trees → below it mulched vegetable beds with a buried 2 ℓ bottle beside a plant → a
washing basin tipped onto a mulched ring of banana-shaped plants (generic broad leaves) → a
cut-away of soil at the bottom showing water soaking down into dark soil like a sponge. Four
large soft numbered bands across the top (①②③④).

items.title: Artwork for F-P08 · How much rain from your roof?
items.brief:
Top: a single square metre of ground marked with four pegs and
string, a rain cloud over it, and one 1-litre bottle beside it. Middle: a simple house with a
corrugated roof, a measuring tape along the length and width at ground level, rain falling, and
a row of identical 20 ℓ buckets lined up beside a tank. Bottom: a tank close-up — gutter with a
gentle fall, a vertical first-flush pipe that fills before water reaches the tank, a lid, a tap
raised on a stand above a bucket, and an overflow pipe leading to a planted swale.

items.title: Artwork for F-P09 · A swale on the level line
items.brief:
A large cross-section of a slope (uphill on the left). A trench on
the level line (about 40 cm wide, 30 cm deep) with water standing in it and blue arrows
soaking down and sideways under the mound; the dug soil forms a mound on the DOWNHILL side,
mulched with grass and planted with a small tree and bushes whose roots reach towards the wet
zone. Rain falls at the top; water runs down, stops in the ditch. A small inset (top right) of
the swale from above following a curved line of pegs, with a stone-lined spillway at one end.

items.title: Artwork for F-P10 · Soil is alive
items.brief:
Top 55%: a cut-away of soil under a mulched vegetable, magnified:
earthworms, a beetle, white fungus threads wrapped around roots, dark crumbs with air gaps,
water droplets held in the crumbs, tiny dots for microbes. Bottom 45%: four small panels for
the hand tests — (a) a hand squeezing a ball of soil, three results: falls apart / ball that
crumbles / sticky ribbon between finger and thumb; (b) a clear jar with settled layers (coarse
at the bottom, fine in the middle, finest on top, bits floating); (c) a nose near a handful of
dark soil; (d) a spade-deep square hole with worms being counted on fingers.

items.title: Artwork for F-P11 · Build a compost heap
items.brief:
A tall cut-away of a 1 m compost heap with visible layers from the
bottom: sticks/stalks (with air gaps), thick yellow-brown dry grass, a thin green layer of
fresh cuttings and peels, a dark thin manure layer, a sprinkle of soil, a watering can pouring
— repeated three times, topped with a dry-grass blanket and a long stick pushed into the
middle. Beside it, four round icons: a green leaf, a brown dry leaf, a water drop, and an air
swirl. Bottom strip: a hand squeezing a handful with two drops falling; a hand feeling the
warm stick; a fork turning the heap.

items.title: Artwork for F-P12 · Liquid manure & worm farm
items.brief:
Top half: a 20 ℓ drum cut-away with a sack of manure hanging from a
stick across the top, water to near the brim, a lid beside it; then a cup of dark liquid
poured into a watering can with ten cups of clear water (show 1 dark cup + 10 clear cups in a
row); then the can watering the soil around a plant (not the leaves). Bottom half: a two-level
worm farm made of stacked crates/buckets: top with shredded paper bedding, red worms and
peels; bottom catching dark liquid through holes; a sack on top; placed in shade.

items.title: Artwork for F-P13 · Beds that hold water
items.brief:
Top 60%: a cut-away trench bed 1 m wide in the ground with a gogo
reaching to the middle from one side and a young man from the other (arms showing the reach).
Layers visible like a sandwich: sticks and cardboard at the bottom, manure, green, dry grass,
soil — repeated — topsoil with young plants on top, mulch, and a small lip at the edges holding
water. A ruler shape on the side shows the depth (no numbers — the label does it). Bottom 30%:
a round keyhole bed from above — a circle with a notch path to a woven compost basket in the
centre, a person standing in the notch.

items.title: Artwork for F-P14 · Grow strong seedlings
items.brief:
Left column: two groups of generic seeds — large seeds going
straight into a bed; small seeds going into a tray. Centre: three buckets (compost, sand, soil)
pouring into a basin through a sieve; a tray of recycled containers (yoghurt tubs, egg box,
toilet rolls) with holes; a finger making a hole twice as deep as a seed is wide (show the
seed beside the hole for scale). Right column: a sequence of the same seedling — in light
shade being watered with a fine rose → moved into more sun over several days (sun icons
increasing) → planted into a bed at the same depth in late-afternoon light, mulched.

items.title: Artwork for F-P15 · Planting plan: spacing & rotation
items.brief:
Top 55%: a 1 m × 2 m bed from above with plants placed in a
triangle pattern — a middle line of large round cabbage-like heads, rows of leafy plants on
either side, a dense row of thin onion-like shoots at one end, small flowers at the corners; a
1 m spacing stick lying along the edge with notches. Bottom 40%: a four-part wheel (like a
clock with four segments) with arrows turning clockwise: a bean pod → a leafy head → a round
fruit (tomato/pumpkin shape) → a root (carrot/beetroot shape) → back to the bean pod.

items.title: Artwork for F-P16 · Healthy garden, fewer pests
items.brief:
A tall wooden ladder with seven rungs, filling the height of the
poster. Beside each rung, a small scene (bottom to top): 1 dark soil with worms and a strong
plant; 2 a mixed bed with flowers; 3 a person looking under a leaf; 4 hands picking a
caterpillar, a toilet-roll collar round a seedling, a net over a bed; 5 a ladybird, a bird, a
frog, a spider on its web; 6 a 2 ℓ bottle with garlic and chilli beside it and a spray bottle;
7 (top, greyed and smaller) a generic chemical container with gloves and a mask.

items.title: Artwork for F-P17 · Food-forest layers & planting a fruit tree
items.brief:
Top 55%: a side view of a small home food forest with seven layers,
generic shapes only: a tall canopy tree, a small fruit tree, a bush, herbs, a spreading ground
cover, a root crop shown in cut-away below the soil, and a climber twining up the small tree.
Fallen leaves on the ground. Bottom 40%: six small steps of planting a fruit tree — a pit with
topsoil and subsoil in separate piles; compost being mixed in; the tree placed so the soil
level matches the bag line; a basin ring of soil; a stake on the windy side with a loose tie;
water and a mulch ring with a gap at the trunk.

items.title: Artwork for F-P18 · Save your seed
items.brief:
Top: two seed packets. Left packet leads to three generations of
similar healthy plants (open-pollinated); right packet (marked with a small generic "F1" style
badge shape — no letters, use a distinct symbol like a double circle) leads to one good plant
then mixed, uneven small plants. Middle left: dry bean pods rattling on the plant, hands
shelling, a bean snapping (dry test). Middle right: a jar with tomato pulp and a white film on
top, then seeds in a sieve under running water, then seeds spread on a plate in the shade.
Bottom: a glass jar with lid on a shelf in shade, a small dish of ash, blank label lines; ten
seeds on a damp cloth, eight sprouted.

items.title: Artwork for F-P19 · Eat the rainbow
items.brief:
A large round enamel plate from above, divided: half filled with
vegetables and fruit of many colours (dark green leaves, orange pumpkin slices, red tomato,
purple beetroot), a quarter with pap, a quarter with beans and an egg. Around the plate, a
family: a gogo, a mother, a toddler on a lap, a school child — eating together. Along the
bottom, four small colour-group icons: a dark green leaf bundle; an orange pumpkin; a bean pod
and peanuts; red/purple fruit.

items.title: Artwork for F-P20 · Money in, money out
items.brief:
Top: three tins on a table with picture icons (a house, a
seedling, a small safe/piggy-bank-like clay pot). Arrows: vegetables being handed to a buyer
and notes coming back into the seedling tin; notes going out of the seedling tin to a seed
packet, a manure bag and a taxi. Middle: an open exercise book with two ruled columns — one
with a green arrow into it, one with a red arrow out of it — and tally marks and simple coin
drawings (no readable text). Bottom: a bunch of spinach with a small price tag shape (blank),
and a simple visual sum: seed + manure + water → one bed → a row of 40 bunches.

items.title: Artwork for F-P21 · My 90-day garden plan
items.brief:
A path drawn from bottom-left to top-right through three stepping
stones. Stone 1: a person mulching and starting a small compost pile beside a tap. Stone 2: the
same person digging one bed north of the house and planting seedlings with a spacing stick.
Stone 3: the same person harvesting leafy greens into a basket, a jar of seed on the windowsill
and a notebook in their pocket. A second smaller person (the buddy) waves from the side with a
phone. Leave three blank rounded boxes beside the stones for writing.

items.title: Our money agreement
items.headline: Our money agreement
items.labels:
1. Made-up families only
2. You may pass
3. It stays here
4. No selling here
5. Every question counts
Question: *What else do we agree?*
items.layout:
Headline top band; art 60% with five callouts round the circle; labels in two rows;
blank space at the bottom (5 cm) for learners' signatures or marks — or a sheet beside it.
items.teach_it:
```
R-P01  Our money agreement                     (≈ 12 min)
1. ASK: When you hear "money", what do you feel? One word each.
2. POINT ①: We use made-up families. Nobody shares their own money.
3. POINT ②: You may say "pass". Nobody asks why.
4. POINT ③: What is said here stays here.
5. POINT ④: Nobody sells anything in this room — not us, not visitors.
6. POINT ⑤: Every question is a good question.
7. ASK: What else must we agree? Add 3. Everyone signs or marks.
KEY: Money is private. Here we learn with made-up families.
```

items.title: The money map
items.headline: Where does money go?
items.labels:
1. Money comes in
2. Our household
3. Money goes out
4. Small leaks add up
Question: *Which is your biggest leak?*
items.layout:
Landscape-style art on a portrait sheet: in-arrows left, out-arrows right; labels
under each side; ④ callout at the drips.
items.teach_it:
```
R-P02  The money map                    (≈ 10 min + 30 min practical)
1. DO: Pour water into a bottle with holes. ASK: Where does it go?
2. POINT ①: Money comes in — grant, wages, piece jobs, garden sales.
3. POINT ②: The household in the middle.
4. POINT ③: Money goes out — food is the biggest arrow.
5. POINT ④: Small leaks add up — airtime, sweets, cold drinks.
6. GROUPS: Build your family's map with beans. 1 bean = R50.
7. ASK: Which pile is biggest? What is left at the end?
KEY: See it before you fix it.
```

items.title: Needs first, wants later
items.headline: Needs first, wants later
items.labels:
1. Need: must have
2. Want: can wait
3. It depends
Question: *When is airtime a need?*
items.layout: Scale centred; labels under each basket; ③ in the middle.
items.teach_it:
```
R-P03  Needs first, wants later                (≈ 5 min + 15 min sort)
1. ASK: What can a family NOT live without?
2. POINT ①: Needs — food, water, school, clinic, soap.
3. POINT ②: Wants — nice, but can wait.
4. POINT ③: It depends — airtime to call the clinic is a need; for games, a want.
5. GROUPS: Sort 24 cards into Need / Want / It depends.
6. DO: Give each group a shock card. What will they cut? Wants first.
KEY: When money is short, cut wants before needs. Each family decides.
```

items.title: Plan the month before it starts
items.headline: Plan the month first
items.labels:
1. Count money in
2. Needs first
3. Save some
4. Farm money aside

6. Keep for surprises
Question: *What did you forget last month?*

Art centred; the six labels line up with the six rows (left of the sheet); question
at the bottom.

```
R-P04  Plan the month first                     (≈ 7 min + 20 min practical)
1. ASK: Before a long journey, what do you do? (plan, save the fare)
2. SAY: A budget is a plan for the month, made BEFORE it starts.
3. POINT ①→⑥ in order: in · needs · save · farm · wants · surprises.
4. GROUPS: Collect your family's month in play money. Put notes on each row, in order.
5. RULE: keep at least R100 for surprises.
6. ASK: What did you cut to keep R100?
KEY: Plan before the month starts. Needs, save, farm — then wants.
```

items.title: Three tins
items.headline: Three tins
items.labels:
1. Home
2. Save

4. Garden money in first
Question: *Who decides the split?*
items.layout: Tins across the middle; labels directly under each tin; ④ callout at the hand.
items.teach_it:
```
R-P05  Three tins                        (≈ 5 min + 10 min practical)
1. TELL: Lerato's R120 went in her purse. By Friday it was gone. No money for seed.
2. ASK: What went wrong? (garden money mixed with home money)
3. POINT ③ ④: Every garden rand goes into FARM first — and into the book.
4. POINT ① ②: Once a week the family decides: some stays FARM, some to SAVE, some HOME.
5. GROUPS: Label three tins. Split R300 of play money. Explain why.
6. ASK: Who should decide? The people who work for it should have a say.
KEY: The farm pays the home — on purpose, not by accident.
```

items.title: Ways to save
items.headline: Ways to save
items.labels:
1. Savings group
2. Bank account
3. Money on phone
4. Tin at home
Question: *Which two will you use?*
items.layout: 2 × 2 grid; label under each panel.
items.teach_it:
```
R-P06  Ways to save                      (≈ 5 min + 15 min scoring)
1. ASK: Where did your grandmother keep money? Honour the answers.
2. POINT ①: Savings group / stokvel: save together, small loans, share-out. Three locks, three keys.
3. POINT ②: Bank or Postbank account: safe; fees; grants can be paid in.
4. POINT ③: Money on the phone: quick; fees; lost phone = risk.
5. POINT ④: Tin at home: quick and free; easy to spend or steal.
6. GROUPS: For each way, a bean for each YES: safe? quick? free? helps me keep saving?
7. SAY: Bank money is protected by law up to R100 000. A stokvel is not — keep records.
KEY: Save somewhere safe AND somewhere quick — often two places.
```

items.title: Keep your money safe
items.headline: Keep your money safe
items.labels:

2. Cover the keypad
3. Never share OTP

number only, not counted as words); five scenes round it with callouts.
items.teach_it:
```
R-P07  Keep your money safe               (≈ 5 min + 15 min game)
1. POINT ①: Your PIN is yours only — not SASSA, not the bank, not family.
2. POINT ②: Cover the keypad. No "help" from strangers at the ATM.
3. POINT ③: The bank SMS number (OTP) is never for a caller.
4. POINT ④: Big prize, big return? It's a hook.
5. POINT ⑤: No shop, lender or relative may keep your card.
6. GAME: Scam or safe? Read 10 cards; groups show red or green.
7. SAY: Money taken? Phone the number on the back of your card NOW. Grant problems: SASSA 0800 60 10 11.
KEY: Nobody real will ever ask for your PIN or OTP.
```

```
R-P08  Write every rand                   (≈ 7 min + 20 min practical)
1. ASK: Lerato's tin has R315. Did she make money? (We can't tell.)
2. POINT ①–⑤: date · what · in · out · balance. One line for every rand, the same day.
3. POINT ⑥: Sold but not paid? Owed to me page — not money in yet.
4. GROUPS: Lerato's week — 10 cards. Move play money, write each line.
5. ASK: Count the tin. Does it match? If not, find the line.
6. ASK: Sold R590. Cash R390. Where is R200? (owed)

```

```
R-P09  Where did the harvest go?          (≈ 5 min + 25 min practical)
1. DO: Put a full basket in the middle. ASK: Where does it go?
2. POINT ①–④: eaten · shared · sold · lost. All four must add up to what you picked.
3. GROUPS: Harvest 5 bunches, weigh one, fill the harvest record for your family.
4. ASK: The family ate 8 bunches. At R12 a bunch, what did they save? (R96)
5. POINT ⑤: Food eaten is money not spent. Write its value.
KEY: Record every harvest. Food eaten is money saved.
```

items.headline: Count every cost
items.labels:
1. Seed

3. Water
4. Transport

Question: *Which cost do people forget?*

Bed centre, six items in a ring; a small legend strip: solid line = cash, dashed

items.teach_it:
```
R-P10  Count every cost                   (≈ 5 min + 20 min sort)
1. ASK: What did it cost to grow this bed? List everything.
2. POINT ①–⑤: seed · compost · water · transport · bands and tools.
3. POINT ⑥ and the dashed lines: your time, your manure, rainwater — free but not free.
4. GROUPS: 12 cost cards → cash costs / free but not free. Add the cash costs with play money.
5. CHECK: Lerato's bed = R510 cash + 44 hours of her time.
6. ASK: Why only R30 for a R90 watering can? (lasts 3 seasons)
KEY: Count every cost — including your own time.
```

items.title: One bunch: cost, price, profit
items.headline: One bunch: cost, price, profit
items.labels:
1. All costs
2. ÷ all bunches
3. Cost of one bunch
4. Floor
5. Market
6. Buyer
Question: *Is your price above the floor?*
items.layout: Two bands: the division (top) and the three price checks (bottom).
items.teach_it:
```
R-P11  One bunch: cost, price, profit     (≈ 10 min + 15 min practical)
1. DO: R40 and 10 bunch tokens. Share the money onto the bunches. (R4 each)
2. POINT ①②③: all costs ÷ all bunches = cost of one bunch. Lerato: R510 ÷ 150 = R3.40.
3. POINT ④: Floor — never sell below R3.40.
4. POINT ⑤: Market — what others charge (check locally).
5. POINT ⑥: Buyer — what this buyer values: fresh, delivered, on time.
6. SUMS: Sales R1 080 − costs R510 = R570 profit. Plus food eaten R480.
7. ASK: Her time — 44 h × R30 = R1 320. Does selling pay her time? Be honest.
KEY: Know your cost of one bunch. Price between the floor and what the buyer values.
```

items.title: Break-even with beans
items.headline: Fill the cup first
items.labels:
1. Season costs cup
2. Each bunch: one bean
3. Full cup: break-even
4. Then profit
Question: *How many bunches fill your cup?*
items.layout: Left-to-right flow: bunches → cup → basket.
items.teach_it:
```
R-P12  Fill the cup first (break-even)    (≈ 5 min + 15 min practical)
1. TELL: Sizanani sells to the creche at R12. Each bunch uses R2 of seed, compost, band.
2. ASK: What does each bunch leave? (R10 = 1 bean)
3. POINT ①: Season costs that don't change: fence R200, cans R100, transport R300 = R600 = 60 beans.
4. POINT ②: Each bunch sold drops one bean in the cup.
5. POINT ③: 60 bunches — the cup is full. Break-even.
6. POINT ④: Bunch 61 onwards — profit.
7. TRY: Price falls to R10. Each bunch leaves R8. How many now? (75)
KEY: Fill the cup first. After break-even, each bunch is profit.
```

```
1. DO: Stick up local month names, September on the left.
2. POINT ①: Money goes out first — seed, compost, before any harvest.
3. POINT ②: Money comes in later, when you harvest.
4. POINT ③: Family big months — December, January school.
5. POINT ④: The pinch month — the tin is lowest. ASK: Which month is hardest here?
6. GROUPS: Dlamini farm tin, Sep–Feb, with play money. Colour red when below zero.
7. POINT ⑤: Save ahead in good months for the pinch month.
```

items.headline: Who buys? What do they want?

```
1. DO: Price board — what prices did you see for a bunch? Why different?
2. POINT ①–⑤: neighbour · spaza · hawker · creche · market.
3. GROUPS: Rank the 6 buyer cards for your family. Why? (amount, price, when paid, quality, distance)
4. DO: Good bunch, bad bunch. Which would you buy?
5. POINT ⑥: Sell together — bigger orders, shared taxi. Needs clear records.
```

items.title: From order to receipt
items.headline: From order to receipt
items.labels:
1. Order
2. Deliver and count
3. Invoice: you owe
4. Paid
5. Receipt: you paid
Question: *Which paper proves payment?*
items.layout: Panels 1–3 in the top row, 4–5 below; big arrow numbers ①–⑤.
items.teach_it:
```
R-P15  From order to receipt              (≈ 8 min + 60 min market day)
1. TELL: The creche says "it was only 20 bunches". What can Lerato show?
2. POINT ①: Order — what, how many, price, when.
3. POINT ②: Deliver — the buyer counts and signs.
4. POINT ③: Invoice — what they owe, by when. Your copy stays in the book.
5. POINT ④⑤: Paid — then a receipt. The buyer keeps the top copy.
6. DEMO 3 minutes, then MARKET DAY: groups buy and sell with role cards.
7. ASK: Who still owes you? Write it on the Owed page. Practise a polite reminder.
KEY: Each paper proves one step. Money owed is not money in the tin.
```

items.title: Borrow wisely
items.headline: Borrow wisely
items.labels:
1. What for?
2. Total cost?
3. Can I pay?
4. Registered lender?
5. What if?
6. Nobody keeps your card
Question: *Is it cheaper to save first?*
items.layout:
Crossroads centre; labels as a numbered list on the right (they are the five
questions + the rule), callouts link to the art.
items.teach_it:
```
R-P16  Borrow wisely                      (≈ 10 min + 20 min practical)
1. TELL: Bongani wants a R3 000 pump now. Where can he get it?
2. POINT ①–⑤: What for? Total cost? Can I pay? Registered? What if?
3. GROUPS: 4 offer cards. Count with play money: gets · pays back · cost.
   (A R1 500 · B R840 · C R450 · D R0). Can the garden pay each month?
4. POINT ⑥: Keeps your ID or card, asks your PIN? Against the law. Walk away.
5. SAY: Check a lender: NCR 0860 627 627. Too much debt: a registered debt counsellor.
6. RULES: Never borrow with interest for food or parties. Borrow less, for less time.
7. The reserve tin: R20 a week → R500 in 25 weeks.
KEY: Compare the total cost, not the monthly payment.
```

A simple house (tin roof, one door) in the centre, drawn like a
container with a small coin pile inside. **Left side:** three thick arrows flowing **into** the

items.title: Artwork for R-P04 · Plan the month before it starts

received for a bunch of spinach (the bunch is in the other hand of a buyer at the edge) and

house tin and the padlock tin. A family (grandmother, mother, young man) stands below, looking

items.title: Artwork for R-P06 · Ways to save

items.title: Two ways to listen
items.brief:

at her watch; the farmer's gestures slow and stop, shoulders drop. 7–8 s: soft wipe. 8–15 s:
same farmer; the mentor puts the phone in her bag, squats to his level, nods; the farmer
straightens, gestures more, points to a bed. 15–16 s: hold, loop.

items.title: I do · We do · You do
items.brief:

farmer watches. 7–15 s: the farmer plants with the mentor's hand guiding hers. 15–22 s: the
farmer plants three alone; the mentor steps back, hands in pockets. 22–24 s: they sit and talk
(no speech bubbles); loop.

Three mentors-in-training (a young woman, an older man, a young man) waiting politely
at a farmer's gate; one waves; the farmer walks towards them from the garden; a dog sits calmly
by the gate. 16:9.

items.title: The observer stands back
items.brief:
In a garden: the mentor and the gogo kneel planting seedlings together (the gogo's
hands on the plant); a recorder writes in a notebook nearby; an observer stands 3 m back with a
clipboard, watching the gogo's face. 16:9.

items.title: Before and after pairs (set of 4)
items.brief:
Four square pairs (8 tiles, 1080 × 1080 each), same viewpoint each pair: (a) bare
cracked bed → mulched bed; (b) empty seedling tray → tray of sturdy green seedlings; (c) an
exercise book with one ruled line filled → many lines filled (lines only, no readable writing);
(d) a 20 ℓ drum with no lid → the same drum with a lid and a tap. Also print as A5 cards for the
Day 1 S4 game.

items.title: Farmer field day
items.brief:
A lively half-day event in a community garden: 30–40 people; a farmer presenting at a
bed with a spacing string; a table of produce with a hanging scale; elders on chairs in shade; a
few children with adults; a buyer (spaza owner in an apron) talking with a farmer. 16:9.

items.title: Weighing a harvest
items.brief:
Close view: the gogo hangs a bunch of spinach on a hand-held hanging scale; the youth
beside her holds a phone (blank screen) and she holds an exercise book open (blank ruled lines).
16:9.

items.title: Invoice handed to a buyer
items.brief:
At a spaza counter (shelves of generic tins and bags, no brands), a farmer hands a
bundle of bunches and a paper invoice (blank lines) to the shop owner; a carbon invoice book lies
open on the counter. 16:9.

items.title: A mentor on the WhatsApp classroom
items.brief:
The mentor sits on a low wall at the edge of a garden in the late afternoon, holding a
phone to her mouth to record a voice note, a printed A5 card and notebook on her lap. Blank
screen. 16:9.
