**Animations (NEW)**

items.title: A real observed farm visit
items.brief:
On a Day 2 farm visit (host and trainees consent in writing): a wide shot of a trio at
work in a host garden — the farmer's hands on the task, the observer standing back. No children.
Landscape, natural light, faces optional (backs and hands are fine). Replaces M-IMG-05 when available.

items.title: A real cluster visit circle
items.brief:
The share circle at a cluster visit, taken from outside the circle, all participants
consenting (green-sticker holders out of frame). Landscape. Replaces M-P11-ART on the slide when available.

items.title: Walk beside
items.headline: Walk beside, not in front
items.labels:
1. In front: I lead
2. Behind: I push
3. Beside: we walk
items.layout: Headline top band; three scenes in the art area with ①②③; label strip below.
items.teach_it:
1. ASK: Who was the best helper you ever had? What did they do?
2. POINT ①: the helper in front — when is that right? (new skill, danger)
3. POINT ②: behind — how does a farmer feel when pushed?
4. POINT ③: beside — the farmer chooses the path; the mentor walks with them.
5. GROUPS: sort your helper stories under ① ② ③.
KEY: Walk beside. The farmer chooses the path.

items.title: The mentor's promise
items.headline: The mentor's promise
items.labels:
1. I listen first
2. Only real promises
3. Your story stays private
4. No gifts that bind
5. I keep you safe
items.layout: Hand centred; five callouts on the fingers; labels in a list below.
items.teach_it:
1. ASK: What happens when a mentor promises a tank and none comes?
2. POINT ①–⑤ one by one; ask for one example of each.
3. GROUPS: one "What would you do?" card each (day-1.md S1).
4. SAY: Tea is hospitality. A chicken is a gift that binds.
5. SAY: Harm to a child or adult — tell your supervisor the same day.
KEY: Promise only what you can do.

items.title: Listen with ears, eyes and heart
items.headline: Listen with ears, eyes, heart
items.labels:
1. Ears: let them finish
2. Eyes: same level
3. Heart: notice feelings
4. Say it back
items.layout: Scene centre; four callouts; labels below.
items.teach_it:
1. PAIRS: 1 minute of bad listening. How did it feel?
2. POINT ①: count to 3 before you speak.
3. POINT ②: sit or squat at their level; phone away.
4. POINT ③: "You sound tired of this."
5. POINT ④: "So the water runs out in week two…"
6. TRIADS: speaker · listener · observer, 3 rounds.
KEY: Say it back, then ask. No advice yet.

items.title: The question ladder
items.headline: Climb the question ladder
items.labels:
1. Closed: yes or no
2. Open: how, what
3. Deeper: what happens
4. Their plan: what else?
items.layout: Ladder runs bottom-left to top-right; callouts on rungs; labels beside each rung.
items.teach_it:
1. ASK: "Did you water?" — what answer do you get? (yes)
2. POINT ②: "How do you water the beds?"
3. POINT ③: "What happens to the water after you pour it?"
4. POINT ④: "What could you try? What else?"
5. GROUPS: climb 10 closed-question cards.
6. SAY: Start with "What are you proud of?"
KEY: The best answer is the one the farmer finds.

items.title: I do · We do · You do
items.headline: I do · We do · You do
items.labels:
1. I do: show once
2. We do: together
3. You do: watch quietly
4. Talk: what worked?
items.layout: Four panels in a Z order; callouts ①–④; labels below each panel.
items.teach_it:
1. DO: explain the A-frame by talking only. Ask a volunteer to build it. Why was it hard?
2. POINT ①: show once, slowly, say each step.
3. POINT ②: the farmer's hands, your help.
4. POINT ③: hands in pockets. Say nothing.
5. POINT ④: What went well? What was hard?
6. Result: demonstrated alone = Demonstrated. Anything else = Needs further support.
KEY: One skill per visit. The farmer's hands.

items.title: The action agreement
items.headline: One action, one owner, one date
items.labels:
1. What?
2. Who?
3. By when?
4. How will we know?
items.layout: Handshake centre; the four vignettes in the corners with ①–④.
items.teach_it:
1. ASK: "I'll try to mulch" vs "I will mulch the 2 front beds by Friday" — which happens?
2. POINT ①: one small action, the farmer's words.
3. POINT ②: a named person.
4. POINT ③: before the next contact.
5. POINT ④: what we will see.
6. GROUPS: fix "Farmer must improve the soil".
KEY: What · Who · By when · How we'll know.

items.title: The Visit Hand
items.headline: Five fingers, five steps
items.labels:
1. Look back
2. Walk and look
3. Listen and ask
4. Try it together
5. Agree and record
items.layout: Hand fills art area; labels curve beside each finger with ①–⑤.
items.teach_it:
1. ASK: hold up your hand — what are the 5 steps of a visit?
2. POINT ①: "Last time you planned… show me." (5–10 min)
3. POINT ②: "What are you proud of?" Farmer leads. (15 min)
4. POINT ③: "What would help most right now?" (10 min)
5. POINT ④: one skill, I do · We do · You do. (15 min)
6. POINT ⑤: what · who · by when · how we'll know. Write it at the farm. (10 min)
KEY: Never cut the ring or little finger.

items.title: What to look at, stage by stage
items.headline: What to look at, stage by stage
items.labels:
1. Baseline
2. Planting and spacing
3. Growth and pests
4. Harvest and weigh
5. Selling surplus
6. Review and seed
items.layout: Six equal panels in a row; callouts ①–⑥; labels below.
items.teach_it:
1. ASK: Where are most of your gardens today? Point.
2. POINT ②: the spacing string — check one row on every establishment visit.
3. POINT ④: weigh, don't count bunches.
4. SAY: Pick 3–5 checks for the stage and the farmer's priority (playbook §5).
5. SAY: ★ = a Course 1 skill — look for it.
KEY: Look at what matters for this stage.

items.title: Traffic light: who needs me most?
items.headline: Who needs me most?
items.labels:
1. Red: every 2 weeks
2. Amber: every month
3. Green: cluster plus phone
items.layout: Traffic light left third; scenes and labels right; ①②③.
items.teach_it:
1. ASK: 40 farmers, 20 working days — can you see all every week?
2. POINT ①: not started, crisis, missed 2 contacts, asked for help.
3. POINT ②: growing, needs further support.
4. POINT ③: skills demonstrated, could host.
5. SAY: Re-sort every month. The colour is private.
6. GROUPS: sort the 40 case cards.
KEY: Nobody goes a month without a contact.

items.title: A mentor's week
items.headline: A mentor's week
items.labels:
1. One cluster a day
2. Cluster visit weekly
3. Farthest first
4. Friday: phone, records
items.layout: Map top 55%; weekday strip below; callouts ①–④.
items.teach_it:
1. DO the sum: Red × 2 + Amber = visits needed.
2. POINT ①: each weekday belongs to one cluster — less travel.
3. POINT ②: the cluster visit rotates A → B → C → D.
4. POINT ③: start far, work back towards home.
5. POINT ④: phones, records, planning, buddy.
6. GROUPS: draw your week on the A3 grid.
KEY: Plan by cluster and route, and leave spare time.

items.title: The cluster visit
items.headline: Learn in a neighbour's garden
items.labels:
1. Welcome and register
2. Host's tour
3. Try it together
4. Share circle
5. Everyone agrees one action
items.layout: Scene with ①–⑤ in visit order; labels below.
items.teach_it:
1. ASK: How many farmers can you reach in 2½ hours this way? (8–12)
2. POINT ①: register, consent, last month's actions.
3. POINT ②: the host shows what works; ask the host open questions.
4. POINT ③: 2–3 stations, groups of 3–4.
5. POINT ④: farmers answer each other first.
6. POINT ⑤: one action each, aloud; next host.
KEY: The host teaches; the mentor asks. Rotate the host.

items.title: Phone check-in
items.headline: Ten minutes on the phone
items.labels:
1. Greet
2. Look back
3. Show me
4. What's next?
5. Date
items.layout: Two halves; five numbered steps down the centre line.
items.teach_it:
1. PAIRS: sit back to back — like a phone.
2. POINT ①: "How are you and the family?"
3. POINT ②: "Last time you planned… how did it go?"
4. POINT ③: "Can you send a photo — or describe it?"
5. POINT ④–⑤: "What will you do this week? I'll call on…"
6. SAY: Write it — phone log or Record visit.
KEY: Green farmers stay connected with 10 minutes a month.

items.title: The season journey
items.headline: Six months with our farmers
items.labels:
1. Baseline
2. Establish
3. Grow
4. Harvest
5. Sell
6. Review
items.layout:
Path across the full width; ①–⑥ at stops; a legend row for the contact symbols
(symbols only, words typeset: visit · cluster · phone · field day).
items.teach_it:
1. ASK: What happens in a garden over six months?
2. POINT ①–⑥: one sentence per stop (playbook §7).
3. POINT the symbols: which contact fits which farmer?
4. SAY: Field days at first harvest and at the review.
5. GROUPS: put your cluster visits on the path.
KEY: Every month, every farmer, one contact at least.

items.title: Two tracks, same records
items.headline: Phone or paper: same records
items.labels:
1. Weigh and record
2. Money in, out
3. Keep the slip
4. Invoice the buyer
5. Read the season
items.layout: Two lanes top to bottom; callouts ①–⑤ on the shared objects.
items.teach_it:
1. ASK: She sold spinach for a month. Did she make money? How would she know?
2. POINT the lanes: app or paper — same outcome.
3. POINT ①: weigh first, then write kilograms.
4. POINT ②–③: every rand in and out; every cost has a slip.
5. POINT ④: an invoice is not a payment.
6. POINT ⑤: the month-end summary or the report.
KEY: Paper is never second best.

items.title: When it gets hard
items.headline: When it gets hard
items.labels:
1. Stay calm
2. Listen
3. What can they do?
4. Who else can help?
items.layout: Footprints ①–④ across the art; labels below.
items.teach_it:
1. ASK: What hard things happen to our farmers? (drought, theft, conflict, drop-out, waiting for inputs)
2. POINT ①: breathe, sit down.
3. POINT ②: say back, no blame.
4. POINT ③: their options, their choice — start small.
5. POINT ④: neighbours, the group, programme, clinic, SAPS, helplines.
6. SAY: Danger now: SAPS 10111 · Childline 116 · GBV 0800 428 428.
KEY: You are a mentor, not a rescuer. Refer and record.

items.title: Show me what changed
items.headline: Show me what changed
items.labels:
1. Before
2. After
3. The date
4. What we saw
items.layout: Before/after top two-thirds; notebook scene below; ①–④.
items.teach_it:
1. ASK: How would a funder know this garden changed?
2. POINT ①②: same spot, same angle — mark the spot at the first visit.
3. POINT ③④: close an action with a date and evidence.
4. SAY: Not done is information: "What got in the way?"
5. GROUPS: which photo pair proves the action?
KEY: An action is closed only with a date and evidence.

items.title: Artwork for M-P01 · Walk beside
items.brief:
Three small scenes stacked on a dirt path between vegetable beds.
Top: a person with a clipboard striding ahead, farmer trailing behind, head down (in front).
Middle: the same person behind the farmer, pointing and pushing (behind). Bottom, largest and
in full colour: mentor and farmer walking side by side, the farmer pointing at a healthy bed,
the mentor listening, both smiling. Top two scenes muted (Hairline/grey), bottom in full palette.
Sun in the north; shadows fall south.

items.title: Artwork for M-P02 · The mentor's promise
items.brief:
An open hand (palm facing viewer) drawn large, each finger with a small
round picture above it: an ear; a hand pushing away a box of goods; closed lips with a finger
(privacy); a hand politely refusing a live chicken while accepting a cup of tea; a shield over a
child and a woman. Warm Paper background, Ochre circles.

items.title: Artwork for M-P03 · Listen with ears, eyes and heart
items.brief:
The mentor squatting at the same level as the gogo farmer who sits on
an upturned 20 ℓ drum beside a bed. The mentor's phone is in her bag (visible, put away). The
gogo is talking with open hands; the mentor nods. Three soft Ochre circles highlight the
mentor's ear, her eyes (looking at the bed the gogo points to), and her hand on her chest.

items.title: Artwork for M-P04 · The question ladder
items.brief:
A wooden ladder leaning against a fruit tree. On the bottom rung the
farmer stands with arms folded; on each higher rung the farmer climbs higher, looking more
engaged; at the top the farmer is reaching for a ripe fruit with a smile. The mentor steadies the
ladder at the bottom. Four rungs highlighted with Ochre numbers.

items.title: Artwork for M-P05 · I do · We do · You do
items.brief:
Three panels left to right on one strip of garden, the same pair each
time, laying a knotted spacing string along a bed and planting seedlings. Panel 1: mentor plants,
farmer watches. Panel 2: both kneeling, the farmer's hands on the seedling, the mentor's hand
guiding. Panel 3: the farmer planting alone; the mentor standing back with hands in pockets,
watching. A small fourth panel: both sitting, talking (speech-shape without words).

items.title: Artwork for M-P06 · The action agreement
items.brief:
The mentor and farmer shaking hands over a garden bed at the end of a
visit. Around them, four corner vignettes: a bundle of dry grass mulch on a bed (what); the
farmer's grandson carrying grass (who); a wall calendar with one square circled (by when — no
numbers); the same bed later, covered in mulch, with the mentor looking and the farmer pointing
(how we'll know).

items.title: Artwork for M-P07 · The Visit Hand
items.brief:
A large open hand (brown skin tone, palm towards viewer, fingers
spread). In each fingertip a small round scene: thumb — mentor and farmer looking at a mulched bed
together (look back); pointing finger — the pair walking between beds, farmer pointing; middle
finger (tallest) — the pair sitting in shade talking; ring finger — both kneeling, farmer's hands
planting; little finger — handshake with a notebook. Palm: a simple garden seen from above.

items.title: Artwork for M-P08 · What to look at, stage by stage
items.brief:
One garden drawn six times in a row, left to right, as it changes over
a season: (1) boundary pegged, beds marked, drum at the roof; (2) beds planted with a spacing
string laid along one row, seedlings in a tray, mulch; (3) plants growing, a person checking
under leaves, a bucket of liquid manure; (4) harvest basket on a hanging scale, a family plate;
(5) a bunch of spinach being handed to a buyer at a spaza counter, a notebook; (6) seed drying on
a sack, jars, the mentor photographing the garden from the same spot as panel 1. Sun in the
north in every panel.

items.title: Artwork for M-P09 · Traffic light: who needs me most?
items.brief:
A tall traffic light made from three stacked round shapes, each with a
small scene beside it. Top (Red, with a triangle pattern for B&W): a bare, dry garden and a
worried farmer — the mentor walking towards them. Middle (Amber/Ochre, with dots): a half-planted
garden, farmer working. Bottom (Green/Leaf, with stripes): a lush garden and a farmer showing
neighbours around. A small calendar icon next to each (two marks, one mark, one mark + a phone).

items.title: Artwork for M-P10 · A mentor's week
items.brief:
A simple map of four villages (A, B, C, D drawn as four clusters of
houses with gardens — letters typeset on the layout, not in the art) around a small town with a
taxi rank. Five columns below the map, one per weekday, each showing a small figure of the
mentor: Monday under a tree with a group of 10 farmers (cluster visit) then walking to 2
houses; Tuesday to Thursday walking a curved route to 3 houses in one cluster; Friday at a table
with a phone and a notebook. Dotted route lines on the map from the farthest house back to the
taxi rank.

items.title: Artwork for M-P11 · The cluster visit
items.brief:
A host farmer's garden with 10 farmers of mixed ages and genders. In
one corner the host gogo leads a tour, pointing at a mulched bed; in the middle, three small
groups of 3–4 kneeling at different stations (spacing string, seedling tray, a bucket); at the
front, everyone sitting in a circle in the shade of a tree; the mentor sits in the circle, not
standing. A cable-tied poster shape on the fence (blank).

items.title: Artwork for M-P12 · Phone check-in
items.brief:
Split scene. Left: the mentor at a table with a basic phone to her ear
and a notebook. Right: the farmer in his garden, phone to ear, looking at a mulched bed; a second
small inset shows him taking a photo of the bed with a smartphone. A thin line (like a sound
wave) connects the two phones.

items.title: Artwork for M-P13 · The season journey
items.brief:
A winding path across the poster through six "stops", each a small
garden scene matching M-P08's stages, from bare ground (left) to harvest and seed jars (right).
Along the path, small symbols show contact types: a single pair walking (individual visit), a
circle of people under a tree (cluster visit), a phone (check-in), and at stops 4 and 6 a big
gathering with a table of produce (field day). Sky changes from spring to high summer.

items.title: Artwork for M-P14 · Two tracks, same records
items.brief:
A path that splits around a tree into two lanes and joins again. Left
lane: the youth holds a smartphone (screen blank), showing it to the gogo farmer. Right lane: the
gogo writes in an exercise book with a pencil; an envelope of slips and a carbon invoice book
beside her. Both lanes pass the same four objects: a hanging scale with a bunch of spinach, a
till slip, a bunch handed to a buyer, a small bar chart shape. They meet at a garden gate where
the mentor waits.

items.title: Artwork for M-P15 · When it gets hard
items.brief:
A dry garden with wilting plants and an empty drum. The farmer sits on
the ground, head in hands. Four steps shown as footprints leading to him: the mentor breathing
calmly; the mentor sitting beside him listening; the farmer standing, pointing at one small bed
he can save; a small group of neighbours arriving with a wheelbarrow of grass mulch. No clinic or
police imagery needed.

items.title: Artwork for M-P16 · Show me what changed
items.brief:
Two matching views of the same bed from the same spot, side by side:
left "before" — bare, cracked soil; right "after" — mulched, planted at even spacing, healthy.
Below, the mentor and the farmer look at a notebook together; the farmer points at a line. A
small wall-calendar square with a tick. Same fence post in both views so the viewer sees it is
the same place.
